data.title: China's gold imports said to have surged to record $209B through Oct.
data.description:
• China’s gold imports reportedly surged to a record $209B so far this year, in an unprecedented buying spree that followed a promise by top officials to make their country into the world’s marketplace instead of just its factory.
  • The shift began in January — the same month Vice Premier He Lifeng made that vow in front of a crowd at Davos — as the value and volume of bullion imports more than doubled from the month before.
  • Non-monetary gold purchases continued climbing in the 10 months through October, reaching a historical high that’s equivalent to nearly 8% of overall imports in the period, the latest data showed Friday, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: MSCI reportedly discussed avoiding Indonesia downgrade with Prabowo, Dalio
data.description:
• MSCI Inc. (MSCI) CEO Henry Fernandez conveyed a willingness to consider alternatives to a two-step downgrade of Indonesia’s stock-market status in recent direct talks with President Prabowo Subianto, Bloomberg reported.
  • Fernandez and Prabowo spoke for more than an hour on a Nov. 10 conference call brokered by Ray Dalio, the billionaire founder of hedge fund Bridgewater Associates, the report said.
  • Dalio, who has acted as an informal adviser to Prabowo’s government, joined the call, as did Rosan Roeslani, the CEO of the Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara. A few other minders and close aides were also dialed in, the report added.
  • Indonesia faces scrutiny from MSCI after the global index provider ​warned the country's stocks could be removed from its indexes in 2027 ‌and ⁠the market relegated two steps down from an emerging market to "standalone" status, bypassing the frontier rating.
  • Fernandez said during ​the call ⁠that MSCI did not necessarily intend to downgrade Indonesia and instead would continue to advise Indonesian officials on the ⁠steps ​they would need to take to ​ensure they meet the necessary standards, according to the report.

data.title: Monday's Economic Calendar
data.description:
8:30 AM Chicago Fed National Activity Index 

The Chicago Fed National Activity Index, or CFNAI, is a monthly index that tracks overall economic activity and inflationary pressures.

9:45 AM PMI Composite Flash 

The flash Composite Purchasing Managers' Index, or PMI, provides an early estimate of current private sector output by combining information obtained from surveys of around 1,000 manufacturing and service sector companies. 

Marginally slower but still good expansion expected in the November flash with manufacturing at 54.5 versus 54.9 in the October final. Services seen at 55.7 versus 56.1 in the October final.

11:00 AM  Export Inspections

This report contains a weekly summary of grains weighed for export in metric tons, including totals for the current and previous market year to date.

1:00 PM 2-Yr Note Auction

Treasury notes are sold at regularly scheduled public auctions. The competitive bids at these auctions determine the interest rate paid on each Treasury note issue.

data.title: Trump calls for Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang amid China probe
data.description:
• President Donald Trump late on Monday said bringing Jensen Huang back to Nvidia (NVDA) would be the best move for both the company and the United States.
  • “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang,” he said in Truth Social post.
  • The comments come as U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that the U.S. is seeking answers from Nvidia (NVDA) on its chip sales to China and ​will find out who was in charge of compliance at the ‌company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
  • "We've been in touch with the ​temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do ​need answers. ... It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because ⁠we want to know what the culture was," Bessent told the CBS ​program "Face the Nation."
  • Once the most valuable company, Nvidia is now fourth behind Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOG). The chipmaker's shares fell 14% on Friday and are down ~34% this year.

data.title: Asian markets extend losses after Wall Street selloff; U.S. futures rebound
data.description:
Asian equity markets traded mostly lower on Monday, extending last week's global technology-led selloff as concerns over AI valuations continued to weigh on investor sentiment. South Korea's Kospi bore the brunt of the selling, falling more than 5%, even as U.S. equity futures rebounded following Wall Street's steep weekly losses. Japan's markets remained closed for a public holiday.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng (HSI) declined 0.64%, China’s Shanghai Composite (SHCOMP) slipped 0.96%, Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged down 0.20%, while India’s Sensex (SENSEX) lost 0.47%.

China’s state-backed funds invested a record 90B yuan ($13.5B) in ETFs on Friday, stepping up efforts to support the country’s stock market as a prolonged selloff pushed the benchmark CSI 300 Index into bear-market territory.

Australia's composite PMI falls to the lowest level in over five years.

Spot gold rebounded around 1.7% to $3,584 an ounce, recovering after a sharp 8.9% decline last week. Brent crude slipped 0.30% to $92.29 a barrel, while WTI fell 0.18% to $83.26, extending last week's losses. 

Wall Street tumbled on Friday, pushing the S&P 500 into correction territory, with the index down 3.7% and the Nasdaq falling 5.3%. However, U.S. futures rebounded in Asian trading on Monday, with S&P 500 futures up 2.05%, Nasdaq 100 futures gaining 2.88%, and Dow futures up 1.44%.

data.title: Waymo pauses San Francisco service from Monday amid storm warning
data.description:
• Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Waymo is said to be temporarily pausing ride-hailing services across San Francisco and the Peninsula starting Nov. 23 at 4am PT, ahead of the severe weather forecast for the week.
  • San Francisco officials have been in conversations with Waymo for several days about the forecasted heavy storms and high tides, Mayor Daniel Lurie said in an earlier X post.
  • Lurie has warned that an “extremely serious” situation was about to hit the city, based on National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and National Weather Service forecasts, and urged people to consider not traveling for the holiday.

data.title: Beijing steps up market rescue with record 90B yuan ETF purchases
data.description:
China’s state-backed funds invested a record 90B yuan ($13.5B) in ETFs on Friday, stepping up efforts to support the country’s stock market as a prolonged selloff pushed the benchmark CSI 300 Index into bear-market territory.

The purchases across nine ETFs associated with China’s so-called national team exceeded the previous record of 87 billion yuan set during the April 2025 market downturn triggered by US tariffs, according to Bloomberg.

The Harvest CSI 300 ETF attracted a record 23B yuan in inflows, while the ChinaAMC SSE 50 ETF received an all-time high of 21.7B yuan.

The latest buying comes as Chinese equities face mounting pressure from an artificial intelligence-led technology selloff. The CSI 300 has declined in all but two weeks since August, with state-backed purchases yet to reverse the broader market downturn.

Alongside the ETF purchases, China's three main stock exchanges announced measures to support market liquidity. The Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges will lower the minimum margin financing requirement for investors buying securities with borrowed funds to 80% from 100%, effective November 30. The change, approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, reverses a tightening introduced in January.

The outstanding balance of margin trades fell 1.9% on Friday, marking its steepest decline since July 20, according to the report.

The Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges also announced plans to reduce trading fees, while the Shenzhen Stock Exchange proposed introducing a market-making mechanism on its ChiNext startup board to help curb share-price swings and improve market liquidity.

The record ETF purchases and easing of margin financing requirements underscore Beijing’s efforts to support market liquidity and investor confidence amid persistent selling pressure.

data.title: South Korea's KOSPI drops 5% as AI fears trigger broader stock sell-off
data.description:
South Korean stocks extended their losses on Monday, with the benchmark KOSPI falling as much as 5.41% intraday as investors retreated from technology and semiconductor shares amid concerns over AI valuations, heavy infrastructure spending and potential U.S. export restrictions.

The KOSPI had already dropped 5.21% on Friday. At an intraday level of 4,606.44, the benchmark was down approximately 21.4% from its November 2 close.

Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) fell nearly 6% at one point during Monday's session, while SK hynix (SKHY) also lost around 6%. Over the past month, Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) has declined ~20.1%, while SK hynix (SKHY) has lost around 18.1%, reflecting sustained pressure on South Korea's semiconductor sector.

Among other major companies, Samsung Biologics fell 5.61% on Monday, LG Energy Solution declined 3.26%, Hyundai Motor (HYMLF) dropped 4.90%, Kia (KIMTF) lost 4.42%, KB Financial Group (KB) fell 3.87%, Shinhan Financial Group (SHG) declined 3.94%, and Samsung Life Insurance dropped 4.18%.

The sell-off followed Friday's sharp decline in U.S. technology and semiconductor stocks, as investors questioned the returns on heavy AI infrastructure spending and grew concerned about tighter U.S. semiconductor export restrictions. 

South Korean authorities are preparing a 10T won ($6.8B) stock-market stabilization fund to curb the sell-off and restore investor confidence. The government will also ease restrictions on listed companies’ daily share-buyback orders for three months from November 24, while regulators step up surveillance of illegal short selling and monitor margin loans and potential forced liquidations.

Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said Monday that South Korea's economy could grow in the upper-3% range next year if current trends continue, citing strong exports and investment gradually supporting domestic demand. Consumer inflation is also expected to ease in 2027 as global oil prices stabilize.

However, Lee warned that AI regulation, geopolitical tensions, rising global interest rates, and semiconductor-sector volatility remain key risks. Given South Korea's reliance on chip exports, prolonged weakness in technology demand could weigh on the broader economy.

South Korea-focused ETFs came under significant pressure in November. The Direxion Daily MSCI South Korea Bull 3X ETF (KORU) plunged 54.10% through November 20, while the KICK Korea Semiconductor Index ETF (KCHP) and xETFs Korea AI Semiconductor ETF (KSMH) fell 26.90% and 24.89%, respectively.

Among broad-market funds, the iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) declined 18.70%, while the Franklin FTSE South Korea ETF (FLKR) lost 18.08%. The Matthews Korea Active ETF (MKOR) dropped 18.82%, and the PLUS Korea Manufacturing Core Alliance Index ETF (KMCA) fell 23.07%. The PLUS Korea Defense Industry Index ETF (KDEF) recorded a comparatively smaller decline of 13.51%.

data.title: Australia's Composite PMI falls to lowest level in over five years
data.description:
• Australia’s Flash Composite PMI fell to 46.1 in November from 48.2 in October, marking the second consecutive month of contraction and the steepest decline in private-sector activity since August 2021.
  • Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.7 from 49.6, its lowest since December 2024, while Services PMI declined to 46.2 from 48.5, its steepest contraction since November 2023. Output and new orders across the private sector fell at their fastest pace in over five years.
  • Employment and foreign demand declined, while input and output price inflation eased; business sentiment fell to a three-year low.

data.title: Clariant, CD&R in talks to acquire chemicals firm Ashland - Bloomberg
data.description:
Clariant AG (CLZNF) (CLZNY) and private equity firm CD&R are in discussions to buy chemicals maker Ashland (ASH).

The Swiss specialty chemicals company and the PE firm are negotiating an all-cash deal that values Ashland close to its share price on Friday, according to a Bloomberg report on Sunday, which cited people familiar with the matter. A transaction could come together as soon as the coming days.

No final decision has been made, and talks could fall apart, or another suitor could still emerge, the people told Bloomberg. 

Ashland and Clariant declined to comment. A spokesperson for CD&R didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

A potential deal comes as activist investors have been pushing for months for Ashland (ASH) to explore a sale. In August, Ashland confirmed an agreement with activist investor Ancora Holdings to expand the chemical maker's board.

Last month Dealreporter said that CD&R was partnering with Clariant (CLZNF) for a bid for Ashland (ASH).
